claims.text: In depression, catatonia (like psychosis) marks severe illness.
claims.quote: Psychosis and catatonia indicate severe depression, as does a melancholic syndrome.

claims.text: Medical workup (history, exam, and sometimes labs or brain imaging) for new-onset or qualitatively different symptoms.
claims.quote: Assessment by history, physical examination, and sometimes laboratory testing or brain imaging (1) is required for patients with New-onset psychiatric symptoms (ie, no prior history of similar symptoms) Qualitatively different or unexpected symptoms in a patient with a known or stable psychiatric disorder

claims.text: Head CT for new-onset symptoms, delirium, headache, recent trauma or focal neurologic findings.
claims.quote: Head CT: Patients with new-onset psychiatric symptoms or with delirium, headache, history of recent physical trauma, or focal neurologic findings (eg, weakness of an extremity)

claims.text: Screening labs: CBC; electrolytes with calcium and magnesium, BUN, creatinine; ESR or CRP; HIV; urinalysis.
claims.quote: Complete blood count Electrolyte levels (including calcium and magnesium), blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine Erythrocyte sedimentation rate or C-reactive protein HIV testing Urinalysis

claims.text: EEG to exclude nonconvulsive status epilepticus, which can cause altered mental status, rigidity and hyperthermia.
claims.quote: Nonconvulsive status epilepticus can cause altered mental status, rigidity, and hyperthermia. Electroencephalography should be obtained to exclude status epilepticus.

claims.text: With fever and rigidity on an antipsychotic, test for NMS complications: electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, glucose, calcium, magnesium, CK and urine myoglobin.
claims.quote: There are no confirmatory tests, but patients should have testing for complications, including serum electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, glucose, calcium, magnesium, and creatine kinase, urine myoglobin, and usually neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid analysis.
